1.title: feat: add Urdu (ur-PK) language support (#11869)
1.body: Adds Urdu language support to the editor. ### **Changes** - **`packages/excalidraw/locales/ur-PK.json`** — complete Urdu translation (610/610 strings, matches `en.json` structure) - **`packages/excalidraw/i18n.ts`** — registered `ur-PK` in the `languages` list with `rtl: true` (Urdu is a right-to-left script) - **`packages/excalidraw/locales/percentages.json`** — added `"ur-PK": 99` so the language passes the completion threshold and appears in the language picker but it's actually work not just for passing the threshold ### **Behavior** - Urdu now appears in the language dropdown labeld as "Urdu" - Setting the language flips the UI to RTL via `setLanguage` (`document.documentElement.dir = "rtl"`) which is build previously - Untranslated keys fall back to English via the existing fallback chain ### **Testing** - `yarn test:typecheck` - Verified all 610 translation keys match `en.json` (no missing/extra keys) - Manually selected Urdu in the language picker and confirmed RTL layout + Urdu strings render correctly

3.title: fix: support Enter to edit selected groups (#8511)
3.body:
## Summary

Fixes the Enter-key group editing bug reported in #8511.

The app already allowed group editing through the double-click interaction, but the keyboard path did not enter the same edit mode when a group was selected and Enter was pressed.

## Root cause

The Enter-key handler was missing the selected-group branch. It handled text, linear, and frame editing flows, but skipped the equivalent group-edit flow.

## Fix

- Added the missing selected-group check in the Enter key handling flow
- Ensured the app enters group-edit mode consistently for selected groups
- Kept nested group Escape behavior intact

## Verification

```bash
cd /workspaces/excalidraw && yarn vitest run packages/excalidraw/tests/selection.test.tsx --testNamePattern='enter edits a selected group|esc unwinds nested group editing before deselecting'
```

Result:
- 1 file passed
- 2 tests passed
- 0 failed

+### QA / Bug Triage Report
+
+#### Summary
+This report documents a defect affecting the Enter-to-edit interaction for selected groups in Excalidraw. The issue was reproduced in the local project environment and was confirmed to be caused by a missing keyboard interaction path rather than a rendering or sandbox-related condition.
+
+The defect manifested as follows:
+- A group could be selected successfully
+- Double-click editing worked correctly
+- Pressing Enter did not enter group-edit mode
+- The keyboard flow failed to follow the expected group-edit state transition
+
+No code sandbox was used in the reproduction, diagnosis, or validation of this issue.
+

+#### Test 01 — Original report evidence
+Reviewed

+The reported issue was assessed against the observed interaction model. The reproduction showed that the selected group did not respond correctly to the Enter key despite the equivalent double-click interaction functioning normally. This created an inconsistency in expected keyboard behavior and identified the issue as a logic gap in the interaction handler.
+
+Observations:
+- Group selection was functional
+- Double-click edit flow was correct
+- Enter key path did not transition into group-edit mode
+- The issue was isolated to the keyboard input flow
+
+#### Test 02 — Root cause validation
+Confirmed match

+A detailed review of the event handling logic confirmed the root cause. The Enter-key handler included branching for:
+- text editing

8.title: fix(editor): make element body clickable for links on mobile in view mode
8.body:
## Summary
On desktop, when `viewModeEnabled` is true (e.g. a shared/read-only view or presentation mode), clicking anywhere on an element's bounding box opens its link. On mobile, `isPointHittingLink` explicitly excluded this path via a `!isMobile` guard, so only the small (~12px) link icon was clickable — inconsistent with desktop and easy to miss on a touch screen. This closes #9637.

## Fix
Remove the `!isMobile &&` guard in `packages/excalidraw/components/hyperlink/helpers.ts` (`isPointHittingLink`), so the "whole bounding box is clickable in view mode" path applies equally on mobile and desktop. Outside view mode, behavior is unchanged on both platforms (only the link icon is hit-testable).

This is safe because the existing drag/scroll protection in `App.tsx#handleElementLinkClick` (the `draggedDistance > DRAGGING_THRESHOLD` check, plus requiring both pointerdown and pointerup to hit) is already platform-independent and applies identically regardless of `isMobile`.

## Test plan
- Added `packages/excalidraw/components/hyperlink/helpers.test.ts` (5 tests) covering: no link → false; selected element → false; mobile view-mode body tap → true (regression for #9637); desktop view-mode body click → true (unchanged); outside view mode, only the icon is hit on both platforms.
- `yarn test:typecheck`, `yarn test:code`, `yarn test:other` all pass with zero errors/warnings.
- Full `packages/excalidraw/tests` suite (49 files / 796 tests): 786 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed.
- [ ] Manual verification on a real mobile/touch device is recommended before merge (not performed here — jsdom only).

9.title: fix(packages/excalidraw): complete cross-document runtime ownership
9.body:
## Summary

- load Excalifont for the empty-scene Welcome UI in the editor document
- keep standard and hyperlink tooltips in the trigger/editor document and use its viewport/timers
- construct decoded image elements through the mounted editor window
- schedule throttled pointer work and animated trails through the mounted editor window
- keep independent animation-frame/timer queues per window and release an idle window as soon as its final animation stops

## Context

This is a focused follow-up to #11974. A single Excalidraw runtime can now render into another document, but several paths still reached the runtime's global `document`, `window`, `Image` constructor, or frame/timer scheduler. That leaves fonts, tooltips, decoded image elements, and scheduled editor work in the wrong realm for iframe, popout, and similar multi-document integrations.

The scheduler mismatch becomes user-visible when the window in which the shared runtime was evaluated is occluded or throttled. In an Obsidian popout entering macOS native fullscreen, pointer events continued to reach the popout, but hand-tool updates remained queued until pointer-up and laser trails did not render. Throttled handlers now receive the mounted editor window, while `AnimationController` keeps separate pending queues for each supplied window without changing its default single-window API.

The existing modal portal already targets `excalidrawContainer.ownerDocument.body`, so this PR does not alter modal behavior.

## Validation

- `yarn test:app packages/common/src/utils.test.ts packages/excalidraw/tests/animation.test.ts --update --watch=false` (20 tests passed)
- `yarn test:typecheck`
- `yarn build:common`
- `yarn build:excalidraw`
- ESLint and Prettier on all newly touched files
- manual Obsidian integration test on macOS: hand panning, laser, element dragging, eraser/lasso trails, native-fullscreen entry/exit, and popout teardown

12.title: fix(search): keep results order stable when elements move on canvas
12.body:
fix #9503

## Problem

The search results list reorders itself while you drag elements around (or anyone else changes the canvas). `handleSearch` sorts matches by `element.y`, and the search effect re-runs whenever the scene nonce changes — which happens on every drag — so the list reshuffles under your hands.

Per @dwelle in the issue: results should keep a constant ordering so the list doesn't change while you're working through it.

## Approach

The initial ordering for a query stays as-is (top-to-bottom by `y`), but the order is now **captured** when a query is (re)searched and replayed on subsequent scene-driven re-searches:

- matches are keyed by `elementId:matchOffset` (stable while elements move),
- on scene-triggered re-search the fresh match set is re-sorted into the captured order,
- new matches (elements added mid-search) are appended at the end in their natural `y` order,
- changing the query resets the order snapshot.

So dragging never reshuffles the list, but you still get sensible top-to-bottom ordering when you start a search, and newly matching elements still show up.

## Testing

- added regression test `should keep search results order stable while elements move` in `tests/search.test.tsx` (mutates an element's `y`, waits out the debounce, asserts the match order is unchanged)
- `vitest packages/excalidraw/tests/search.test.tsx` — 6/6 pass
- eslint + prettier clean

21.title: feat: Persistent per-tool style settings
21.body:
# Excalidraw Per-Tool Settings (#10666) - Report & PR Prep

## Phase 2 — Root Cause Analysis

### Current Behavior
In Excalidraw, style properties (color, stroke width, fill, etc.) are stored as top-level properties in the `AppState` (e.g., `currentItemStrokeColor`). When an element is drawn, it inherits these values. When an element is selected, the global `AppState` is updated to match that element's styles.

### Root Cause
Styles propagate across tools because there is only **one shared state** for each property in `AppState`. The switching logic for tools (`setActiveTool`) focuses on the visual active state and cursor but does not transition the styling configuration.

### Design Intent
The current architecture prioritizes simplicity and a "global brush" metaphor. However, as Excalidraw evolves towards more complex sketching (High-frequency pen use), this global state becomes a source of friction for users who frequently switch between a "Pencil" (for sketching) and "Shapes" (for diagramming).

---

## Phase 3 — Design Decision

### Choice: Option B (Hybrid Per-Tool Styles)
Each tool remembers its last-used style. When switching tools, the "Brush" is swapped for the tool's specific preset. If no preset exists (first use), it inherits the current global style.

**Justification:**
- **Low Cognitive Load**: Users don't need to manually save presets.
- **Natural UX**: Mimics "Picking up a different pen."
- **Backward Compatible**: Doesn't change the data structure of elements.

---

## Phase 7 — PR Description

### Table of Contents
- [Problem](#problem)
- [Solution](#solution)
- [Design Decisions](#design-decisions)
- [How to test](#how-to-test)

### Problem
Changing styles in one tool (e.g., set Pencil to Blue) affects all other tools (Rectangle becomes Blue). This forces users to constantly re-adjust styles when switching between different types of work (e.g., sketching vs. annotation).

### Solution
Implemented a tool-scoped style cache within `AppState`.
- New property: `currentItemStyles: Record<ToolType, Partial<AppStateStyleProperties>>`.
- Automatic sync: Global styles are persisted to the active tool's cache on every change and tool switch.
- Automatic restoration: Preferred styles are restored when switching "to" a drawing tool.

### Design Decisions
1. **Drawing Tools Only**: Persistence is skipped for "Selection", "Hand", and "Eraser" to keep the experience predictable.
2. **Real-time Sync**: We sync both on property change and tool switch to ensure state isn't lost on page reloads.
3. **Implicit Presets**: No new UI buttons are added. The tool "just remembers" what you last did with it.

### How to test
1. Draw a **Red Rectangle**.
2. Switch to **Pencil**, change color to **Blue**.
3. Switch back to **Rectangle**. It should be **Red**.
4. Change **Rectangle** to **Bold**.
5. Switch to **Arrow**. It should have its own last-used width (or default), not necessarily Bold.
6. Verify settings persist after page refresh.

Closes #10666

23.title: fix(eraser): guard against undefined in groupsToErase for ungrouped elements
23.body:
Fixes #11260.

`element.groupIds.at(-1)!` returns `undefined` for ungrouped elements (empty `groupIds` array), polluting the `groupsToErase` Set with `undefined` entries. Added a `element.groupIds.length > 0` guard before the `.at(-1)` access in both the erase and restore paths of `updateElementsToBeErased`. Added 3 tests covering ungrouped, grouped, and mixed elements. All 468 existing tests pass.

24.title: fix(clipboard): await copy before delete in cut action to prevent data loss
24.body:
Fixes #11262.

`actionCut.perform` calls async `actionCopy.perform` without awaiting it, then immediately deletes elements. If the clipboard write fails, elements are gone but the clipboard is empty - silent data loss.

Awaited the copy result and only delete if copy succeeded. On failure, error is surfaced and elements are preserved. Reproduced by blocking all 3 clipboard fallback methods (navigator.clipboard.write, writeText, document.execCommand). All 465 existing tests pass.

25.title: feat: parse pasted Markdown into styled handwritten elements
25.body:
This PR makes paste understand Markdown. Pasting a Markdown document now produces styled canvas elements in the handwritten font, instead of raw syntax markers like `##`, `**`, and `| --- |` scattered across plain text lines.

## Problem

Copying notes from any Markdown editor into Excalidraw currently dumps the source syntax onto the canvas. Headings keep their `#` prefixes, tables arrive as pipe-and-dash soup, and code fences show up as literal backticks. The structure the user wrote is lost, and cleaning it up by hand takes longer than retyping.

## What this does

On paste, the text is checked for structural Markdown. When it matches, each block becomes canvas elements that keep the sketchy look:

- Headings become larger text elements. `#` maps to 32px, `##` to 28px, `###` to 24px, all in the default handwritten font.
- Unordered list items are rendered with a bullet. Ordered lists keep their numbering.
- Blockquotes become muted gray text.
- Fenced code blocks become a light gray box with monospace (Cascadia) text lines inside.
- Tables are rendered as a real grid: an outer border, a filled header row, a horizontal separator under every row, and vertical separators between columns. Every cell is its own editable text element.
- Inline syntax (`**bold**`, `_italic_`, `` `code` ``, links, images) is stripped to its readable text.

All generated elements are regular Excalidraw elements, so the result can be selected, moved, and edited cell by cell like anything else on the canvas.

## What this does not affect

Plain text without structural markers takes the existing paste path unchanged. The detection requires a heading, list marker, blockquote, code fence, table separator row, or horizontal rule on its own line. Sentences containing `#` or dashes mid-line (for example "The C# language") do not trigger it. Spreadsheet paste, Mermaid paste, image paste, and element paste all run before this branch and keep their current behavior. `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+V` (plain paste) also bypasses it.

## Implementation

- `packages/excalidraw/markdown.ts` (new): dependency-free block parser and element builder. Exports `isMaybeMarkdown` and `convertMarkdownToElements`.
- `packages/excalidraw/components/App.tsx`: one branch in `insertClipboardContent`, placed after the spreadsheet check. Elements are laid out from the origin and positioned at the paste cursor through the existing `addElementsFromPasteOrLibrary`, the same way the Mermaid path works.
- `packages/excalidraw/markdown.test.ts` (new): covers the detection guard (both positive and negative cases) and the conversion of each block type. 10 tests, all passing.

`tsc` passes with zero errors.

## Example

Pasting this:

```markdown
| Feature | Status | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Auth | Done | Anna |
| Payments | In progress | Ben |
```

renders a bordered grid with a header fill and per-row separators, in the handwritten font. Headings, lists, quotes, and code blocks follow the styles described above.

26.title: fix(editor): re-apply scroll constraints during pointer-drag panning
26.body:
Fixes #11910

Drag-pan and both scrollbar-drag paths passed a plain object read from this.state to viewport.translate. translate applies the scroll constraints in a second, function-form setState, so a throttled pointermove re-based on the pre-clamp scroll and a locked viewport drifted out of its box. Keyboard paths already used the updater form, which is why only dragging escaped.

27.title: fix: upgrade shell-quote to 1.8.4 (CVE-2026-9277)
27.body:
## Summary
Pin `shell-quote` to `1.9.0` in `dev-docs` (transitive dependency, via `@docusaurus/core > react-dev-utils`) to fix CVE-2026-9277.

**Version note**: `1.8.4` is the first version containing the CVE-2026-9277 fix (vulnerable range is `>= 1.1.0, <= 1.8.3`, per [GHSA-w7jw-789q-3m8p](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w7jw-789q-3m8p)). We pin to `1.9.0` instead of the minimum `1.8.4` because `1.9.0` is newer and also carries the fix for a separate DoS advisory in `shell-quote`'s `parse()` (quadratic-complexity DoS, CVE-2026-13311, first patched in `1.9.0`). So the title should be read as "upgrade to at least 1.8.4, pinned to the newer 1.9.0" — sorry for the confusion in the original title.

## Vulnerability
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **ID** | CVE-2026-9277 |
| **Severity** | CRITICAL |
| **Scanner** | trivy |
| **Rule** | `CVE-2026-9277` |
| **File** | `dev-docs/yarn.lock` (dependency: `shell-quote`) |
| **Assessment** | Present in dependency tree, not confirmed reachable |

**Description**: shell-quote: shell-quote: Arbitrary code execution via command injection due to unescaped line terminators

## Reachability

`shell-quote` here is a transitive, build-time-only dependency of `dev-docs`'s Docusaurus tooling (`@docusaurus/core > react-dev-utils > shell-quote`, confirmed via `yarn why shell-quote`). `dev-docs` is the docs site (`docusaurus build`/`start`) and is not part of the root Yarn workspace (`workspaces: ["excalidraw-app", "packages/*", "examples/*"]`) — it never ships in the Excalidraw editor bundle or in the deployed docs site's runtime JS. Real-world severity here is therefore closer to "hardening the docs build toolchain" than the CRITICAL/user-facing risk the advisory implies for `shell-quote` in general; the scanner's own assessment ("not confirmed reachable") agrees. Still worth fixing since it removes a vulnerable transitive dependency from the tree for any future consumer.

## Changes
- `dev-docs/package.json` — add `shell-quote: 1.9.0` to `resolutions`
- `dev-docs/yarn.lock` — regenerated via `yarn install` inside `dev-docs/` so the resolution actually takes effect. `dev-docs` has its own lockfile (it's outside the root workspace), so the `resolutions` entry alone was inert until the lockfile was regenerated — the original commit here missed this step; `#11873` is a comparison PR that did include the matching lockfile update from the start.

## Behavior Preservation
The change is scoped to 2 files on the vulnerable path; it only tightens handling of untrusted input and leaves valid inputs unaffected.

---
*This change addresses a pattern flagged by static analysis. The code path handles user-influenced input and the fix reduces the attack surface against both manual and automated exploitation.*

---

28.title: fix: upgrade websocket-driver to 0.7.5 (CVE-2026-54466)
28.body:
## Summary
Upgrade websocket-driver from 0.7.4 to 0.7.5 to fix CVE-2026-54466.

## Vulnerability
| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **ID** | CVE-2026-54466 ([GHSA-xv26-6w52-cph6](https://github.com/faye/websocket-driver-node/security/advisories/GHSA-xv26-6w52-cph6)) |
| **Severity** | CRITICAL (CVSS v4 9.2) |
| **Scanner** | trivy |
| **Rule** | `CVE-2026-54466` |
| **File** | `yarn.lock` (dependency: `websocket-driver`) |

**Description**: `websocket-driver` parses the WebSocket frame length header into a JS number. Because JS uses 64-bit floats, a client can send an ever-growing length value that loses precision, causing the driver to misread subsequent payload bytes as message data ("message corruption via abuse of protocol length headers"). Affects all versions `< 0.7.5`; no workaround exists pre-patch. Fixed in 0.7.5 by rejecting frames whose length header exceeds the configured max message length.

## Reachability
`yarn why websocket-driver` traces the only path into the tree as:

```
excalidraw-app -> firebase -> @firebase/database -> faye-websocket -> websocket-driver
```

So it ships as part of the `firebase` npm package that `excalidraw-app` depends on (for storage), not via webpack/build tooling. That said, `excalidraw-app/data/firebase.ts` only imports `firebase/app` and `firebase/storage` — it never imports `firebase/database` (Realtime Database), which is the only Firebase product that pulls in `faye-websocket`/`websocket-driver`. So the vulnerable code is present in the installed dependency tree but isn't on any path Excalidraw actually executes or bundles today. Pinning it is still worthwhile since `yarn.lock` would otherwise happily resolve the `>=0.5.1` range to a vulnerable version for this or any future consumer.

## Changes
- `package.json`: add `"websocket-driver": "0.7.5"` to `resolutions`
- `yarn.lock`: collapses `websocket-driver@>=0.5.1` onto the pinned `0.7.5` (no second copy installed), so the pin actually takes effect on install

---
*Automated security fix by [OrbisAI Security](https://orbisappsec.com)*

29.title: test(editor): re-enable flip tests for curves outside min/max points
29.body:
Closes #11709.

Eight tests in `flip.test.tsx` were skipped behind `//TODO: elements with curve outside minMax points have a wrong bounding box!!!` — they cover flipping arrows and lines whose curve extends beyond their min/max points, rotated and unrotated, horizontally and vertically.

That TODO no longer holds. The bounds of such an element now account for the curve rather than the declared width/height, so the flip keeps the bounding box dimensions and the tests pass.

## Verification

- Re-enabled the eight tests: `flip.test.tsx` passes 46/46, and the result is stable across repeated runs.
- Full suite is unaffected: 122 files, 1868 tests passing.
- Checked the underlying claim directly rather than trusting the passing tests alone: for an arrow whose curve reaches well past its declared height, `getElementAbsoluteCoords` and `getElementBounds` both return bounds that include the curve.

This matches what @ezemskov reported on the issue after reproducing the fixture by hand.

Only the skips and the stale TODO comments are removed; no product code is touched.

### Reproduced on current master (e1bb9ff8)

Applying the same eight un-skips to a clean checkout of master and running the file:

```
 RUN  v3.0.6

 ✓ packages/excalidraw/tests/flip.test.tsx (46 tests) 6938ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  46 passed (46)
   Duration  14.39s
```

### The re-enabled tests are not vacuous

Measuring the `createLinearElementsWithCurveOutsideMinMaxPoints` fixture directly, comparing point-only bounds against the curve-aware bounds returned by `getElementAbsoluteCoords`:

| | width | height |
| --- | --- | --- |
| declared on the element | 591.28 | 69.33 |
| bounds from points only | 591.28 | 69.33 |
| bounds including the curve | 652.67 | 72.67 |
| curve overshoot | +61.39 | +3.34 |

The curve overshoots the declared box by 61px horizontally, and the point-only bounds come out identical to the declared width/height. So the fixture does overshoot as its name claims, and `checkElementsBoundingBox` is comparing curve-aware bounds on both sides of the flip. The assertions still have something real to measure.

### On the commit that fixed it

I could not pin it to a single commit, and I would rather say so than guess. The skips and the TODO comments were introduced in 06b45e0c (#5799). Between that and master, `bounds.ts` changed 40 times and `actionFlip.ts` 25 times. Settling it properly means a bisect using this file as the oracle, which I am happy to run if it matters for the merge.

## Summary

Check the restored `migratedElement` instead of the raw input element in `isInvisiblySmallElement`, preventing a secondary crash that kills the entire file import.

Fixes #11925

## Problem

When `restoreElement` throws for a malformed element (e.g. a freedraw with `points: null`), the catch block sets `migratedElement = null` and the element is skipped. However, when the raw input element is later passed to `isInvisiblySmallElement` it tries to read `element.points.length` on the broken element, throwing a second uncaught `TypeError` that kills the entire import — including valid elements.

## Fix

Replace `isInvisiblySmallElement(element)` with `isInvisiblySmallElement(migratedElement)` on line 897. This is safe because:

2. If `restoreElement` threw, `migratedElement` is null and the block is skipped entirely

40.title: fix(element): respect shift-locked angle when dragging line endpoints near bindable elements
40.body:
Closes #11313.

## What was broken

When the user shift-drags a line / arrow endpoint, the orbit-mode binding silently overrides the shift-locked position whenever the endpoint lands within `maxBindingDistance_simple` (~15px) of a bindable element. The endpoint visibly jumps to the element's diagonal / outline midpoint as if the modifier had never been pressed. Per the issue reporter:

> Usually, when you drag points from a line while holding SHIFT, you can draw straight lines (or whatever snap points the application sets) … However, if you try to create lines close to another object, e.g. a rectangle, the handle point you're currently dragging with SHIFT, jumps to where it would be as if you never pressed SHIFT. […] snapping to other objects should be of less priority than the SHIFT modifier.

## Root cause

`getBindingStrategyForDraggingBindingElementEndpoints_simple` in `packages/element/src/binding.ts` runs the already-shift-locked `globalPoint` through `getHoveredElementForBinding`. When a hit lands **outside** the element (`pointInElement` is `false`) it picks orbit binding with:

```ts
focusPoint: projectFixedPointOntoDiagonal(arrow, globalPoint, hit, …) || globalPoint
```

`projectFixedPointOntoDiagonal` rewrites the endpoint onto the bindable element's diagonal / outline midpoint, ignoring the user's locked direction. Downstream, `pointDraggingUpdates` uses that focus point to compute `endLocalPoint` via `updateBoundPoint`, which lands in the returned `positions` map — replacing the naively shift-locked position.

The **inside-binding** branch is fine — it sets `focusPoint = globalPoint`, which IS the shift-locked position, so the modifier is preserved. Only the orbit branch fights the lock.

## The fix

Skip the orbit attempt when `opts.angleLocked` is `true`. Inside binding still kicks in normally when the endpoint really is inside an element. 10 lines, one source file.

With `current.mode === undefined`, downstream in `pointDraggingUpdates` the `else if (start.mode)` branch is skipped, `updates.startBinding` stays `undefined`, and the simulated `nextArrow.startBinding` resolves to `element.startBinding` (preserving prior binding if any). The returned position is the unmodified shift-locked one.

## How to verify manually

1. `yarn start`
2. Draw a rectangle.
3. Draw an arrow nearby. Enter line editing mode (select the arrow + `Ctrl/Cmd + Enter`, or drag an endpoint handle directly).
4. Hold **Shift** and drag an endpoint so it crosses near the rectangle's outline (close enough to bind, but not inside it).

**Before:** the endpoint jumps onto the rectangle's diagonal / midpoint, leaving the line at an unintended angle.

**After:** the endpoint stays on the shift-locked line; no binding is auto-created. Inside binding still works when the endpoint is dragged INTO the rectangle.

## Tests

Two unit-level regression tests added to `packages/element/tests/binding.test.tsx`, exercising the dispatcher in `getBindingStrategyForDraggingBindingElementEndpoints` directly:

- **locked + outside**: shift-locked endpoint lands ~14px outside a bindable rectangle (inside `maxBindingDistance_simple`). Without `angleLocked`, the dispatcher returns `mode: \"orbit\"`; with `angleLocked`, it returns `mode: undefined` — the shift-lock survives.
- **locked + inside**: shift-locked endpoint lands inside the rectangle. Inside-binding's `focusPoint` is the shift-locked `globalPoint` itself, so the modifier is preserved without losing the binding — the `angleLocked` guard does not disable that case.

The first test fails on `main` with `expected undefined, received \"orbit\"`; both pass after the fix. Full sweep (`binding`, `linearElementEditor`, `arrowBinding`): 76 passed / 1 skipped / 1 todo.

## Scope

2 files, `+166 -0` (10 lines fix, 156 lines test). No public API change. `yarn test:typecheck` and `yarn fix` clean.

## Out of scope

Same physical-vs-logical pull-toward-binding mismatch likely exists in the COMPLEX_BINDINGS path (`getBindingStrategyForDraggingBindingElementEndpoints_complex`), which I haven't audited. Happy to extend the fix there in a follow-up if it's affected.

## Summary

43.title: ci(repo): fix broken heredoc in semantic-pr-title.yml
43.body:
## What
Fixes a broken heredoc in the `label-scope` job of `semantic-pr-title.yml`
that causes the job to fail on every PR, and extracts the inline Node
script to its own file to avoid the underlying structural issue.

## The bug
The step embedded a Node.js script via a heredoc inside a YAML `run: |`
block:

```bash
node <<'NODE'
...
          NODE
```

This has two constraints in direct conflict:
- YAML's block scalar requires every line to stay at or above the block's
  base indentation (10 spaces here) or the block scalar ends early.
- Bash's heredoc requires a quoted terminator (`<<'NODE'`) to have **zero**
  leading whitespace.

As written, the terminator satisfied YAML but not bash, so bash never
found the terminator, read to EOF, and fed the rest of the script into
Node's stdin — throwing a SyntaxError and failing the job.

## Fix
Moved the script to `.github/scripts/pr-scope-labels.mjs` and call it
directly with `node`, removing the heredoc (and the conflict) entirely.

## Testing
Ran the extracted script locally against both a scoped and unscoped title:

```bash
PR_TITLE="fix(app,editor): some title" node .github/scripts/pr-scope-labels.mjs
# -> s-app
#    s-editor

PR_TITLE="chore: bump deps" node .github/scripts/pr-scope-labels.mjs
# -> (no output, no scopes matched)
```

Will also confirm the `label-scope` job passes on this PR itself, since
`semantic-pr-title.yml` runs on every pull request.

46.title: Fix accessible-name/visible-content mismatches (WCAG 2.5.3)
46.body:
## What

Three controls whose visible text isn't fully contained in their accessible name — flagged by axe-core's `label-content-name-mismatch` rule (WCAG 2.5.3, Label in Name):

- **Main menu trigger** (`MainMenu.tsx`) — the hamburger icon button had no `aria-label` at all.
- **Toolbar tool buttons** (`Tools.tsx`) — the visible keybinding badge (e.g. "2" on the rectangle tool) wasn't reflected in `aria-label`, so a speech-input user saying what's on the button wouldn't match it.
- **Reset-zoom button** (`actionCanvas.tsx`) — the visible text is the live zoom percentage, not captured by the static "Reset zoom" label.

## Why this matters

WCAG 2.5.3 exists for speech-input users (Dragon, Voice Control, etc.), who activate controls by speaking the text they see. If the accessible name doesn't contain all of the visible text, "click rectangle" or "click 2" can fail even though both are printed right on the button.

## How I found these and verified the fixes

Scanned a real local dev build with a browser-driven axe-core scanner, then re-scanned after each change to confirm the finding actually cleared — rather than assuming a change would work. One early attempt (adding `aria-hidden` to the keybinding badge span) did *not* resolve the finding on re-scan, because this axe rule compares against what's visually rendered, not what's exposed to assistive tech; that attempt was reverted in favor of folding the visible text into `aria-label` instead, which did resolve it.

## Testing

- `yarn test:typecheck` passes
- Manually verified all three controls still read sensibly with a screen reader (label now includes the keybinding/percentage, doesn't duplicate awkwardly)
- Re-scanned with axe-core after each fix to confirm the mismatch is gone

Happy to adjust naming/wording if there's a preferred convention for combining a label with a shortcut hint.

48.title: feat(editor): add shortcut search to help dialog
48.body:
Closes #9276

## Background

#9276 is still open, despite #9279 being merged as a fix for it. The report reads:

> If you press Ctrl + F in the help menu it closes the menu and brings up the global find panel. Some way to search the help panel would be nice

The request was for a way to search the help panel's contents. #9279 read it as "Ctrl+F should not open search while a dialog is open" and added an `openDialog` guard to `actionToggleSearchMenu.perform`.

That guard runs *after* `ActionManager.handleKeyDown` has already called `event.preventDefault()` and `event.stopPropagation()`, so today the key is inert: the browser's find bar is suppressed and the canvas search never opens. Nothing happens at all.

## What this does

Gives the help dialog its own filter over the shortcut list and points Cmd/Ctrl+F at it.

- Adds a `TextField` search box to `HelpDialog`, filtering shortcuts by their `label`.
- `ShortcutIsland` hides itself when none of its rows match; `Section` shows an empty state when no island survives.
- `HelpDialog` registers a capture-phase `keydown` listener on `window` so it claims Cmd/Ctrl+F before the editor's global handler consumes it.

The shortcut rows are authored as JSX rather than data, so matching reads the `label` prop off each child. Restructuring them into a data array would make the filter tidier but would rewrite ~390 lines of unrelated markup, so I kept the change contained to the three wrapper components.

`actionToggleSearchMenu.ts` is intentionally untouched. Since the dialog now consumes the event first, the existing guard never comes into play, and leaving it alone avoids reintroducing the behavior the issue originally complained about.

## Not covered

Cmd/Ctrl+F is still inert in other dialogs (image export, etc.) for the same `preventDefault`-before-bail reason. That's outside this issue's scope and probably deserves its own fix, either by moving the guard into the action's `keyTest` so the event is never claimed, or by giving other dialogs similar handling.

## Test plan

- `packages/excalidraw/tests/helpDialog.test.tsx` (new) covers: Cmd+F focuses the filter, the dialog stays open and canvas search does not open, filtering by label, the empty state, and restoring the full list when the query is cleared.
- `yarn test:typecheck` passes.
- Full suite passes: 123 files, 1865 tests, no snapshot changes.
- New strings added to `en.json` only; other locales come from Crowdin.
